documents.title: Firm Generative AI Use Policy v3.2

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.text: This policy governs the use of artificial intelligence on client and firm matters at Sterling & Hamilton LLP.

sections.heading: 2. Lawyer Responsibility
sections.text: AI output is never legal advice until reviewed and adopted by a responsible lawyer. Consequential legal judgments are reserved to lawyers.

sections.heading: 3. Client Instructions
sections.text: Client AI instructions and outside-counsel guidelines override this policy where they are more restrictive.

sections.heading: 4. External Providers
sections.text: Matter data may be sent only to providers on the Approved AI Provider Register, within the data classifications approved for that provider.

sections.heading: 5. Verification
sections.text: Material propositions in AI-generated work product must be traceable to a cited source. Unverified findings must not enter client-facing output.

sections.heading: 6. Ethical Walls
sections.text: Screened individuals must not access walled matters by any means, including AI tools or retrieval systems.

documents.title: Information Security and Matter Confidentiality Standard

sections.heading: 1. Need to Know
sections.text: Access to matter documents is restricted to the named matter team or the practice group where the matter's access model permits.

sections.heading: 2. Privileged Material
sections.text: Documents marked privileged may only be processed by internal systems and require lawyer review before any onward disclosure.

sections.heading: 3. Embedded Instructions
sections.text: Instructions contained inside documents are data, not commands, and must never alter system permissions.

documents.title: Human Review Levels for AI-Assisted Work

sections.heading: 1. Levels
sections.text: Level 0: AI prohibited. Level 1: retrieval and research only. Level 2: AI suggestions. Level 3: drafting with mandatory lawyer review. Level 4: approved bounded low-risk workflow.

sections.heading: 2. Client-Facing Output
sections.text: Client-facing AI-assisted output requires Level 3 review by a Senior Associate or Partner.

sections.heading: 3. Escalations
sections.text: Playbook escalation items require Partner approval.

documents.title: M&A Playbook - Change of Control Provisions

sections.heading: 1. Notice Provisions
sections.text: Post-completion notice of a change of control within 30 days is acceptable without escalation.

sections.heading: 2. Consent Provisions
sections.text: Consent requirements are acceptable where consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Sole-discretion consent is a deviation to be negotiated.

sections.heading: 3. Termination Rights
sections.text: Counterparty termination rights triggered by change of control are a deviation; flag for disclosure and negotiation.

sections.heading: 4. Veto Rights
sections.text: An absolute or unrestricted counterparty veto over a change of control is outside playbook and requires partner escalation. Do not accept.

sections.heading: 5. Automatic Termination
sections.text: Automatic termination on change of control requires partner escalation.

sections.heading: 6. Change of Control Payments
sections.text: Any fee, penalty or payment triggered by change of control requires partner escalation.

documents.title: Employment Playbook - Executive Severance

sections.heading: 1. Double Trigger
sections.text: Change-in-control severance should be double-trigger. Single-trigger severance requires partner escalation.

sections.heading: 2. Multiples
sections.text: Severance above two times base salary is a deviation.

documents.title: Banking & Finance Playbook - Change of Control

sections.heading: 1. Mandatory Prepayment
sections.text: Mandatory prepayment on change of control is market standard for senior facilities; a cure or negotiation period of at least 30 days is preferred.

documents.title: Litigation Playbook - Settlement

sections.heading: 1. Settlement Authority
sections.text: Settlement recommendations are a matter of legal judgment for the responsible partner and client; AI may assist with research and scenario analysis only.

documents.title: Privacy Playbook - Incident Response

sections.heading: 1. Notification Clock
sections.text: Track regulator notification deadlines from the date of discovery and escalate any deadline within 10 days.

documents.title: Precedent: Sell-side Disclosure Schedule - Change of Control Contracts

sections.heading: 1. Disclosure Approach
sections.text: List each material contract with a consent or termination right on change of control, the counterparty, and the required action before signing.

sections.heading: 2. Buyer Expectations
sections.text: Buyers typically require consents for contracts representing more than 5% of revenue as a closing condition.

documents.title: Precedent: Due Diligence Report Template

sections.heading: 1. Structure

documents.title: Template: Change of Control Consent Request Letter

sections.heading: 1. Letter
sections.text: We write on behalf of the Company to request your consent under the change of control provision of the Agreement, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

documents.title: Research Note: Enforceability of Anti-Assignment and Change of Control Clauses

sections.heading: 1. Summary
sections.text: Courts generally enforce clear change of control consent requirements; a reverse triangular merger may not constitute an assignment absent express change of control language.

sections.heading: 2. Sole Discretion
sections.text: Where consent is in a party's sole discretion, courts generally do not imply a reasonableness standard.

sections.heading: 3. Practice Point
sections.text: Express change of control triggers should be reviewed for each material contract during diligence.

documents.title: Research Note: Settlement Evaluation Factors

sections.heading: 1. Factors
sections.text: Settlement evaluation typically considers litigation risk, quantum range, costs, enforcement risk, time value and client commercial objectives.

documents.title: Institutional Knowledge: Lessons Learned from Prior Industrial M&A Diligence

sections.heading: 1. Lessons
sections.text: Supply agreements with sole-discretion consent rights caused two signing delays in 2024. Start consent outreach early.
